newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall in thin trade by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall in thin trade by lunch break.

text.p: Persistent concerns over first quarter earnings results of finance companies led investors to sell stocks across the board by the lunch break, brokers said.
"The market sentiment wasn't good this morning. Many investors stayed on the sidelines as they were not sure whether current stocks prices have hit bottom yet," said a broker at Securities One.
The SET index declined 5.04 points to 695.19 on 1.8 billion baht turnover by the break.
Brokers said investors expect first quarter results from finance firms to be lower than the same period last year. The results are to due to be released starting today.
"Investor worries about finance earnings along with a lack of fresh, positive news in the market caused investors to stay idle," said the broker at Securities One.
Most of the key sectors were down by the break. The banking sector ranked first in terms of value, dropping 0.45 percent, followed by the commerce sector which rose 1.05 percent.
Siam Makro topped the active list by lunch, rising 2.50 baht to 69.50. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
